title: Petroleum Supply Specialist (Petro Sup SPC)
raw_text:
10-92F. MOS 92F--Petroleum Supply Specialist (Petro Sup SPC), CMF 92 (Eff 202510)
    a. Major duties. The petroleum supply specialist receives, stores, and issues petroleum products, operates and
maintains petroleum equipment, and performs quality control tests on fuel and lubricant. Provide refuel support for
vehicles and aircraft, conduct bulk-to-bulk transfers, and manage fuel inventories, while also ensuring compliance
with environmental and safety regulations to support unit operations and maintain equipment. Duties for MOS 92F
at each level of skill are:
         (1) MOSC 92F1O. Perform basic petroleum laboratory testing, receiving, storing, and issuing petroleum
products. Inspect and test fuel for contamination and adherence to quality control standards. Operate and
maintain petroleum distribution systems, including pumps, tanks, and pipelines. Maintain accurate records of fuel
inventory, consumption, and testing results. Assist in managing fuel storage facilities, ensuring safety and
compliance with regulations. Perform preventative maintenance on petroleum equipment, reporting any
discrepancies or malfunctions. Follow established procedures for handling and disposing of petroleum waste.
         (2) MOSC 92F2O. Perform petroleum quality control testing, analyzing fuel samples and interpret results.
Manage petroleum distribution operations, oversee tank farms and issue points. Maintain accurate inventory
records and prepare detailed reports on fuel consumption and stockage levels. Troubleshoot and repair petroleum
distribution equipment, ensure operational readiness. Train and mentor junior petroleum specialists, enforce
safety regulations and proper procedures. Inspect and evaluate petroleum storage facilities, identify and correct
deficiencies. Coordinate fuel requests and deliveries, ensure timely support for operational requirements.
         (3) MOSC 92F3O. Supervise and manage all aspects of petroleum operations, including quality control,
distribution, and storage. Plan and coordinate fuel supply for large-scale operations, anticipating requirements
and resolving logistical challenges. Analyze fuel consumption data and recommend improvements to optimize
efficiency and minimize waste. Inspect and evaluate petroleum facilities and equipment, ensuring compliance with
safety and environmental regulations. Train and mentor petroleum specialists, developing their technical expertise
and leadership skills. Manage automated petroleum management systems, troubleshooting issues and
maintaining data integrity. Advise commanders on petroleum-related matters, providing expert guidance and
support for mission success.
         (4) MOSC 92F4O. Direct and manage all petroleum logistical functions within a theater of operations or
large-scale organization. Develop and implement petroleum supply plans, coordinating with higher headquarters
and subordinate units. Analyze fuel requirements and allocate resources, ensuring efficient distribution and
stockage. Oversee quality control programs, establishing standards and ensuring compliance with regulations.
Supervise personnel responsible for petroleum storage, distribution, and testing, providing leadership and
technical guidance. Manage automated petroleum management systems, optimizing data flow and improving
operational efficiency. Advise commanders on complex petroleum-related issues, providing expert
recommendations and support for strategic decision-making.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. The petroleum supply specialist must
possess the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of Significant (Gray).
         (2) A physical profile of 211221.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Per AR 600-8-19, promotion to MSG and SGM requires an interim secret eligibility or higher.
         (5) Qualifying scores.
             (a) A minimum score of 86 in aptitude area CL and 85 in aptitude area OF.
             (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0140 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0400
cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0140 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0040 shuttles in Physical Demand
Category in “Significant” (Gray).
         (6) Mandatory formal training. Completion of MOS 92F course conducted under the auspices of the U.S.
Army Quartermaster School); or meet ACASP listed in AR 601-210. Waiver requests can be submitted to the
Office of the Quartermaster Commandant Enlisted Proponent Office at USARMY Ft Lee, VA, 23801. TRADOC
List QM Enlisted Personnel Development usarmy.lee.tradoc.list.qm-enlisted-personnel-development@army.mil.
    c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all MOS)).
         (1) D6--Operational Data Analyst (personnel only).
         (2) 3C--Operational Contract Support (OCS) (SSG thru SGM).
    d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill level are
listed in the following tables:
         (1) Table 10-92F-1. Physical requirements.
         (2) Table 10-92F-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (3) Table 10-92F-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
